notable_absence.finding: This page explains how to set maxConcurrentPartitionMovesPerNode to a chosen N to increase rebalance concurrency ('During the rebalance operations, FTS moves or builds partitions one at a time per node'), but never states the setting's own default numeric value - unlike bleveMaxClauseCount (1024), bleveMaxResultWindow (10000), maxFeedsPerDCPAgent (6), maxReplicasAllowed (3) and slowQueryLogTimeout (5 seconds), all in the same page family, which each state a specific default. A reader can infer from 'FTS moves or builds partitions one at a time per node' that the effective default behavior is N=1, but the page never states this as the setting's literal default value, so it is not captured as a hasDefaultValue relation here.

cross_component_finding: This page explicitly ties three settings together for a single stated goal (fastest rebalance throughput): 'Setting `maxFeedsPerDCPAgent` to 1 with a sufficient FTS memory quota can help to maximize the rebalancing throughput.' That is, maxConcurrentPartitionMovesPerNode (this page), maxFeedsPerDCPAgent and ftsMemoryQuota (both documented on their own dedicated pages elsewhere in this same batch) are presented as a tuning trio for rebalance throughput, not as independent, unrelated knobs - captured above via configurableVia. A fourth setting in this same batch, disableFileTransferRebalance, is thematically about rebalance behavior too (whether partitions are copied between nodes or rebuilt from scratch during rebalance) but is never mentioned on this page, and this page is never mentioned on disableFileTransferRebalance's own page - no page states that connection explicitly, so disableFileTransferRebalance is noted here only as a plausible but UNEVIDENCED fourth member of a broader 'rebalance tuning' theme, per this round's instruction not to force an umbrella concept without a page stating the grouping itself.
